subject: zerogxplode
label: sprites/zerogxplode.spr, in the place of the game's own

R1.reason: Reads as an explosion. Frame 0 is a small ember, frames 1 to 5 a bright core that swells, frames 6 to 10 a lobed fireball with orange-brown billows, and frames 11 to 15 a burn-out. That is the brief's burst, billow into lobes, and burn to nothing.

R2.reason: Each frame is 128 by 128, and the effect fills roughly the central 60 to 80 pixels of every cell, so it neither spills out of the frame nor sits as a speck. Frame 0 is deliberately tiny as a start point. Nothing is clipped at the cell edge.

R3.reason: By eye, the colours read as fire: a white-hot core in frames 2 to 5, yellow-orange in 6 to 7, and brown-orange in 8 to 10 fading to dull brown in 11 to 13. Minor faults: frame 1 has a blue-grey halo around the core, and frames 2 to 5 are blown out to near-white across the whole blob, which loses the lobe shading. Neither is enough to call the colour wrong.

R4.reason: Measured against the explosion class: jitter 1.3 (range 1.04 to 1.48), peak at 0.27 of the run (range 0.22 to 0.71), first frame 0.01 (under 0.22), last frame 0 (under 0.03) and border 0 (within the class). It grows, peaks early, and ends dark. Sixteen frames is what the class takes. Frame 1 is a bright bloom, as the class's flashes are.

R5.reason: Type parallel and format additive, matching the game's file as the harness reads it (gameType and gameFormat agree), the same name, and it reads back as written.
